title: Copying an icon carries the white canvas the export no longer does
goal: Draw an icon on a blank canvas, press Copy (Shift Command C) and paste it somewhere dark, and the white canvas comes with it as solid pixels. Exporting the same icon as a PNG now leaves that canvas out, so the two ways of handing an icon over disagree: the one you save is see-through and the one you paste is not.
notes: Found while finishing an-icon-exported-as-a-picture-can-come-out-with (2026-09-17). Repro of the composite that Copy puts on the clipboard: PHOTONZ_ALLOW_LOCKED_WALK=1 Scripts/playtest.sh /tmp/tmp-png-bg-forced.json --no-build wrote png-export-background-3-file-with-canvas.png, which is the same render EditorState.copyCompositeToClipboard uses (previewRenderer.render(document, store:), no background answer anywhere on that path), and reading its corner back gave top-left (5,5) rgba [255, 255, 255, 255]. The export path in the same walk wrote [0, 0, 0, 0]. The smallest fix is to let the copy take the same SVGExport.Background answer the sheet holds, through PhotonzDocument.drawn(with:flatImages:) (PhotonzCore) the way ExportSizer does; the open question is whether a copy should ask at all or simply always leave a flat canvas out, which is a UX call worth a decision card rather than a guess. PNG and TIFF both go on the pasteboard and both hold alpha.
acceptance: Copying an icon drawn on a blank canvas and pasting it into an app that shows transparency gives an icon with nothing behind it
Copying a screenshot or a captured screen still carries its background exactly as it does today
A walk proves the copied picture is see-through in every corner

log.note: Reproduced, independently of the report. Built the probe, ran /tmp/copy-bg-repro.json with PHOTONZ_ALLOW_LOCKED_WALK=1 (the Mac's screen is locked, and the walk uses no control-name lookups so nothing it does depends on the names a lock takes away): blank 900x700 canvas, a closed pen shape, clearClipboard, then the copyImage action. The walk passed all 20 steps and logged clipboard types [public.png, public.tiff]. Reading the PNG straight off the pasteboard afterwards (swift /tmp/read-clip.swift): size 900x700, and all four corners rgba [255,255,255,255]. The same drawing exported as PNG writes [0,0,0,0]. So the two hand-offs really do disagree, and it is the canvas bitmap, not the shape.

Adversarial review before building, and it did not survive as written. The task's acceptance says copy should simply always leave a flat canvas out. Walking it as a person: (1) Export shows the choice. The sheet has an Include the background checkbox and a swatch of the colour that would go, so the default is visible and one click away from being reversed. Copy has no sheet at all, so the same default becomes silent and, as written, unreachable: there would be NO way left to put the white version on the clipboard. (2) The focus epic is building UI. A wireframe or a screen drawn on a blank white canvas is exactly the same shape of document as an icon on a blank white canvas, and the app cannot tell them apart. Copy that wireframe into a dark themed chat and its dark strokes land on nothing and vanish. That is a real regression for the use we are aiming at, caused by the fix. (3) Screenshots and captures are safe either way: SVGExport.backdrop only fires when the bottom visible layer is one flat colour covering the whole canvas, so a photograph is never touched. (4) Cost is fine: FlatBitmap.color answers a photograph from a 32x32 sample, and only the bottom layer needs reading, so copy does not have to walk twelve megapixels. So the engineering is easy and the product question is the whole task: whether a silent copy should change, and whether the old result stays reachable. That is a UX call, not mine.

left rough: nothing shipped this turn beyond the reproduction and the decision brief. The one implementation detail settled either way and worth keeping: copy should read only the BOTTOM visible layer's bitmap rather than calling FlatBitmap.colors over every layer the way ExportSizer does, because SVGExport.backdrop only ever looks at the bottom one and copy is pressed far more often than Export is. Not filed: it is a line of code inside whichever option wins.

Reproduced (copied PNG reads solid white in all four corners where the exported one reads empty), then stopped at the product question rather than guessing it. The task as filed says copy should always leave a flat canvas out, and that would leave no way at all to copy the white version, which a wireframe drawn on white and pasted into a dark surface needs. Decision card open with four options and a brief with both pictures: queue/decisions/copying-an-icon-carries-the-white-canvas-the-exp-copying-an-icon-should-the-white.md. Recommended B: copy leaves it out, holding Option copies it with.
decision "Copying an icon: should the white canvas come with it?" resolved: Copy leaves it out, holding Option copies it with

Shipped the decided default (commit 0ad13bdd): Copy Merged / Shift Command C on a drawing made on a blank canvas copies with nothing behind it, behind next-copy-leaves-the-canvas-out (on at Next). Only the bottom visible layer is read (FlatBitmap.canvasColor), per the earlier note. Verified: CopyBackgroundTests (5), PlaytestScriptTests parse test, full suite 10640 green, copy-leaves-the-canvas-out-walk green at Next defaults (corners of the PNG on the pasteboard read empty; with the canvas asked for, painted; a screenshot copied with Shift Command C, painted), and the same walk fails at step 21 with the switch off. Nine other copy walks green. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-30-copy-leaves-the-canvas-out.json.

Could not build the Option half of answer B as written. Reproduced with a small AppKit program (/tmp/altkey): an Option alternate of Copy Merged must share the C key, i.e. Option Shift Command C, which is Copy Look. With both present, mainMenu.performKeyEquivalent(Option Shift Command C) returned handled with neither action running (the alternate swallowed it, even disabled and hidden); without the alternate Copy Look fired. So the key is the user's call: decision card opened, recommended a visible row on Control Shift Command C. The app side is ready: EditorState.copyCompositeToClipboard(background: .keep) and the copyImageWithCanvas walk action; the next runner only adds the menu row.

left rough: Copy Merged with a marquee up (copyMergedRegion) still carries white inside the marquee. Deliberately untouched: that copy pastes back into Photonz as a layer, and ⌘A ⌘C ⌘V is documented to duplicate what you see, background included. Not filed: no one has hit it and the decision was about the whole-picture hand-off.

Copy now leaves a blank canvas out (shipped 0ad13bdd, walk green at Next defaults). The Option-held copy WITH the canvas needs Option Shift Command C, which is Copy Look's key: decision card open on where it goes.
